Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 15, verse 1–3:

Tafsir of Surat al-Hijr

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

The discussion of the muqatta'at (the disjointed letters) has already been given at the beginning of the surahs.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾ This is a report about them that they will regret what they were engaged in of disbelief, and will wish that they had been with the Muslims in the worldly abode. [[In T: "in the worldly abode with the Muslims"]]

Al-Suddi related in his tafsir, with his well-known chain, from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and others of the Companions, that when the disbelievers were presented before the Fire, they wished that they had been Muslims.

It has also been said: the meaning is that every disbeliever will wish, at the time of his death, that he had been a believer.

It has also been said: this is a report about the Day of Resurrection, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they will say, "Oh, would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers."﴾ [Al-An'am: 27]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Za'ra', from 'Abdullah, regarding His saying: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾ He said: This refers to the Jahannamiyyun, when they see them coming out of the Fire.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna related to us, Muslim related to us, al-Qasim related to us, Ibn Abi Farwa al-'Abdi related to us, that Ibn 'Abbas and Anas ibn Malik used to interpret this verse: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾ They interpreted it as: On the day when Allah imprisons the people of sins among the Muslims together with the polytheists in the Fire, the polytheists will say to them: "What use to you was what you used to worship in the world?" He said: Then Allah will become angry for them out of the bounty of His mercy, and bring them out, and that is when He says: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾

'Abd al-Razzaq said: al-Thawri informed us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who both said: The people of the Fire will say to the monotheists: "What use to you was your faith?" Then when they say that, He will say: "Bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of an atom." He said: At that point is His saying: ﴿[Perhaps] those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾ [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/299).]]

The same has been related from al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Abu al-'Aliyah and others. There are also raised (marfu') hadiths on this, and the Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said:

Muhammad ibn al-'Abbas, who is al-Akhram, related to us; Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi related to us; Salih ibn Ishaq al-Jahbadh related to us, whom Yahya ibn Ma'in pointed out to me; Mu'arraf ibn Wasil related to us, from Ya'qub ibn Abi Nubatah, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Aghurr, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Some people of [the category of] 'There is no god but Allah' will enter the Fire because of their sins. The people of al-Lat and al-'Uzza will say to them: 'What use to you was your saying, There is no god but Allah, while you are with us in the Fire?' So Allah will become angry for them, and bring them out, and cast them into the River of Life, and they will be cleansed of their burning as the moon is cleansed of its eclipse, and they will enter Paradise, and they will be called in it 'the Jahannamiyyun'." A man said: O Anas, did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? Anas said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire." Yes, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say this.

Then al-Tabarani said: Al-Jahbadh alone narrated it.

[[Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (4821), "Majma' al-Bahrayn"; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/380): "It contains people I do not know."]]

The second hadith: Al-Tabarani also said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us; Abu al-Sha'tha' 'Ali ibn Hasan al-Wasiti related to us; Khalid ibn Nafi' al-Ash'ari related to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah, from his father, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the people of the Fire gather in the Fire, and with them are whoever Allah wills of the people of the qiblah, the disbelievers will say to the Muslims: 'Were you not Muslims?' They will say: 'Yes.' They will say: 'Then what use to you was Islam? You have come to be with us in the Fire?' They will say: 'We had sins, and we were seized for them.' So Allah hears what they said, and commands that those among the people of the qiblah who are in the Fire be brought out. When the disbelievers who remain see that, they will say: 'Would that we had been Muslims, so that we might come out as they came out.'" He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Quran. Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾

[[Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/45): "Al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Khalid ibn Nafi' al-Ash'ari; Abu Dawud said: abandoned (matruk). Al-Dhahabi said: this is an excess in criticism, so he does not deserve abandonment, for Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others narrated from him, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." It was also related by Ibn Abi 'Asim in al-Sunnah (no. 843) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/242) from Abu al-Sha'tha' with it, and al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it."]]

Ibn Abi Hatim related it from the hadith of Khalid ibn Nafi', with it, and added in it: (In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful) instead of the seeking of refuge.

The third hadith: Al-Tabarani also said: Musa ibn Harun related to us; Ishaq ibn Rahawayh related to us, who said: I said to Abu Usamah: Did Abu Rawq (and his name is 'Atiyyah ibn al-Harith) narrate to you: Salih ibn Abi Tarif related to me, who said: I asked Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and said to him: Did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say regarding this verse: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾? He said: Yes, I heard him say: "Allah will bring out some of the believers from the Fire after He has taken His vengeance upon them," and he said: "When Allah has made them enter the Fire with the polytheists, the polytheists will say to them: 'You claim that you were the friends of Allah in the world, so what is the matter with you with us in the Fire?' So when Allah hears that from them, He permits intercession for them, and the angels and the prophets will intercede, and the believers will intercede, until they come out by the permission of Allah. When the polytheists see that, they will say: 'Would that we were like them, so that intercession would reach us and we would come out with them.'" He said: "That is the saying of Allah: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾ They will be called in Paradise the Jahannamiyyun, because of a blackness on their faces. They will say: 'O Lord, remove this name from us,' so He will command them, and they will bathe in the river of Paradise, and that name will leave them." Abu Usamah acknowledged it and said: Yes.

[[Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih (no. 2599) "Mawarid", by way of 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Aban, from Abu Usamah, similar to it.]]

The fourth hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us; al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Narsi related to us; Miskin Abu Fatimah related to us; al-Yaman ibn Yazid related to me, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among them is one whom the Fire will seize up to his knees, and among them one whom the Fire will seize up to his waist, and among them one whom the Fire will seize up to his neck, according to their sins and their deeds. Among them is one who will remain in it a month and then come out of it, and among them one who will remain in it a year and then come out of it. The longest of them in staying there will be as long as the worldly life, from the day it was created until it perishes. When Allah wants them to come out of it, the Jews and Christians, and those of other religions and idols who are in the Fire, will say to the people of monotheism who are in the Fire: 'You believed in Allah, His books and His messengers, so we and you are equal today in the Fire.' Then Allah will become angry for them with an anger He has not shown for anything in the past, and will bring them out to a spring in Paradise." And that is His saying: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾

[[Ibn al-Jawzi related it in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (2/457) by way of al-Baghawi from 'Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Narsi with it. al-Khatib related it in Tarikh Baghdad (6/156) and Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (2/456) by way of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Samiri, from 'Abbad ibn al-Walid al-Ghubari, from Abu Fatimah, from al-Yaman ibn Yazid with it, similar. Ibn al-Jawzi said: "This hadith is not authentic, and in it are a group of unknown narrators."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves﴾, it is a severe threat to them and a firm warning, like His saying: ﴿Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾ [Ibrahim: 30], and His saying: ﴿"Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed you are criminals."﴾ [al-Mursalat: 46]. For this reason He said: ﴿and hope distracts them﴾, that is, from repentance and turning back, ﴿but they will soon know﴾, that is, the outcome of their affair.

So when Allah hears that from them, He permits intercession for them, and the angels and the prophets will intercede, and the believers will intercede, until they come out by the permission of Allah. When the polytheists see that, they will say: 'Would that we were like them, so that intercession would reach us and we would come out with them.'" He said: "That is the saying of Allah: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾ They will be called in Paradise the Jahannamiyyun, because of a blackness on their faces. They will say: 'O Lord, remove this name from us,' so He will command them, and they will bathe in the river of Paradise, and that name will leave them." Abu Usamah acknowledged it and said: Yes.

[[Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih (no. 2599) "Mawarid", by way of 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Aban, from Abu Usamah, similar to it.]]

The fourth hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us; al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Narsi related to us; Miskin Abu Fatimah related to us; al-Yaman ibn Yazid related to me, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among them is one whom the Fire will seize up to his knees, and among them one whom the Fire will seize up to his waist, and among them one whom the Fire will seize up to his neck, according to their sins and their deeds. Among them is one who will remain in it a month and then come out of it, and among them one who will remain in it a year and then come out of it. The longest of them in staying there will be as long as the worldly life, from the day it was created until it perishes. When Allah wants them to come out of it, the Jews and Christians, and those of other religions and idols who are in the Fire, will say to the people of monotheism who are in the Fire: 'You believed in Allah, His books and His messengers, so we and you are equal today in the Fire.' Then Allah will become angry for them with an anger He has not shown for anything in the past, and will bring them out to a spring in Paradise." And that is His saying: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims.﴾

Ibn al-Jawzi said: "This hadith is not authentic, and in it are a group of unknown narrators."]]

As for His saying: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves﴾, it is a severe threat to them and a firm warning, like His saying: ﴿Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾ [Ibrahim: 30], and His saying: ﴿"Eat and enjoy yourselves a little; indeed you are criminals."﴾ [al-Mursalat: 46]. For this reason He said: ﴿and hope distracts them﴾, that is, from repentance and turning back, ﴿but they will soon know﴾, that is, the outcome of their affair.

God says: He did not destroy any town except after the proof had been established against its people and its appointed term had come to an end. And He does not delay any nation whose time of destruction has come beyond its appointed moment, nor do they go ahead of their term. This is a warning to the people of Makkah and a guidance for them to give up the polytheism, obstinacy and deviation in which they are engaged, for which they deserve destruction.

Ibn Kathir said:

Allah (exalted is He) informs us of their disbelief, their insolence and their obstinacy in their saying: ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, surely you are mad!﴾ That is, the one who claims this (revelation). ﴿Surely you are mad﴾ means: in your calling us to follow you and to abandon what we found our fathers upon. ﴿Why do you not bring us the angels?﴾ That is, why do they not bear witness for you to the truth of what you have brought? ﴿If you are of the truthful.﴾ Like the saying of Pharaoh: ﴿Why have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him, or why have the angels not come with him in procession?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 53]. And: ﴿Those who do not hope for meeting Us say: "Why have the angels not been sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" Indeed they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed with a great transgression. On the Day they see the angels, there will be no good tidings that day for the criminals, and they will say: "A forbidding, forbidden barrier."﴾ [Al-Furqan: 21–22].

And similarly He said in this verse: ﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth, and they would not then be reprieved.﴾

Mujahid said concerning His saying: ﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth﴾: "With the message and the punishment."

Then Allah (exalted is He) affirmed that it is He who sent down the Reminder, which is the Qur'an, and it is He who preserves it from alteration and change.

Some scholars held that the pronoun in His saying: ﴿Indeed We are its guardians﴾ refers to the Prophet ﷺ, like His saying: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 67]. However, the first meaning is more preferable, and it is the apparent sense of the context. [And Allah knows best.]

Allah, the Exalted, says, consoling His Messenger regarding the denial of those among the disbelievers of Quraysh who denied him: He sent messengers before him to the earlier nations, and no messenger came to any nation except that they denied him and mocked him.

Then He informs that He caused denial to enter the hearts of the criminals (mujrimun), who were obstinate and arrogant against following guidance.

Anas and al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿Thus We make it enter into the hearts of the criminals﴾ meaning: shirk (polytheism).

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the example of the former peoples has already passed﴾ means: He has already known what Allah did to those who denied His messengers, of destruction and annihilation, and how Allah saved the prophets and their followers in this world and the Hereafter.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 15, verses 14–15:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us of the intensity of their disbelief, their obstinacy, and their stubborn denial of the truth: that even if He opened for them a gate from the sky, and they began to ascend through it, they would still not believe. Rather, they would say: ﴿Our eyes have been dazzled﴾.

Mujahid, Ibn Kathir and al-Dahhak said: "Our eyes have been blocked."

Qatadah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "Our eyes have been seized."

al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "It has been made to look unclear to us, and we have only been bewitched."

al-Kalbi said: "Our eyes have been blinded."

Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Our eyes have been dazzled﴾ means "the drunkard" [[In A: "al-sukr"]] who does not understand.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah mentions His creation of the sky in its height and the bright stars with which He adorned it, for whoever contemplates it. The one who looks at it repeatedly will see in it wonders and striking signs, such that his gaze is bewildered by them. For this reason Mujahid and Qatadah said: "The *buruj* (constellations/mansions) here are the stars."

I say: This is like His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky great constellations and placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon﴾ [al-Furqan: 61]. Some scholars said: the *buruj* are the stations (manazil) of the sun and the moon.

'Ata' al-'Awfi said: The *buruj* here are the fortresses of the guards.

He made the meteors (shuhub) guards for it against the rebellious devils, so that they would not hear the High Assembly (al-mala' al-a'la). Whoever of them rebels and advances to eavesdrop, ﴿a clear flame﴾ pursues him and destroys him. Perhaps he has already conveyed the word he heard to the one below him before the meteor reaches him, and the other takes it and brings it to his companion, as has been stated explicitly in the Sahih, as al-Bukhari said in his tafsir of this verse:

Narrated to us 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah: narrated to us Sufyan, from 'Amr, from 'Ikrimah, from Abu Hurairah, who traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When Allah decrees a matter in the sky, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word, like a chain upon a smooth rock." 'Ali said, and others said: "*Safwan* (smooth rock), it penetrates them. When the fear is removed from their hearts, they say: 'What has your Lord said?' They say: 'The truth, and He is the Most High, the Great.' Then the eavesdroppers hear it, and the eavesdroppers are one above another"—Sufyan described it with his hand, spreading the fingers of his right hand and placing some of them above others—"so the meteor may catch the listener before he throws it to his companion, and it burns him. And sometimes it does not catch him until he throws it to the one below him, and so on, until they cast it down to the earth"—and Sufyan sometimes said: "until it reaches the earth and is cast onto the mouth of the sorcerer or the soothsayer, and he lies with it a hundred lies, and they say: 'Did he not tell us on such and such a day that such and such would happen, and we found it to be true?' Because of the one word that was heard from the sky."

Then He mentions His creation of the earth, His spreading it out, widening it and extending it, and what He placed in it of mountains, valleys, plains and sands, and what He caused to grow in it of crops and fruits in proportion.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿of everything in measured proportion﴾ means known (ma'lum). Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Abu Malik, Mujahid, al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, Abu Salih and Qatadah.

Some said: "Determined by a measure."

Ibn Zayd said: "Of everything that is weighed and measured by a measure." Ibn Zayd also said: "What the people of the markets weigh."

* *

His saying: ﴿And We made for you therein means of living, and [for] those whom you do not provide for﴾ — He mentions that He directed them in the earth toward various kinds of means and livelihoods, and *ma'ayish* is the plural of *ma'ishah*.

* *

His saying: ﴿and those whom you do not provide for﴾ — Mujahid said: these are the animals and livestock.

Ibn Jarir said: they are the slaves, the female slaves, the animals and the livestock.

The purpose is that He, the Exalted, bestows favour upon them by what He facilitated for them of means of gain, ways of acquisition and kinds of livelihood, and by what He subjected to them of beasts they ride, livestock they eat, and slaves and female slaves whom they employ. And their provision is upon their Creator, not upon them; the benefit is theirs, and the provision is upon Allah, the Exalted.

* *

His saying: ﴿and those whom you do not provide for﴾ — Mujahid said: these are the animals and livestock.

Ibn Jarir said: they are the slaves, the female slaves, the animals and the livestock.

The purpose is that He, the Exalted, bestows favour upon them by what He facilitated for them of means of gain, ways of acquisition and kinds of livelihood, and by what He subjected to them of beasts they ride, livestock they eat, and slaves and female slaves whom they employ. And their provision is upon their Creator, not upon them; the benefit is theirs, and the provision is upon Allah, the Exalted.

He, exalted is He, informs that He is the Owner of everything, that everything is easy for Him and within His power, and that with Him are the treasuries of all things of every kind. ﴿And We do not send it down except in a known measure.﴾ He sends it as He wills and as He desires, and for what He has in that of consummate wisdom and mercy toward His servants, not as an obligation. Rather, He has prescribed mercy upon Himself.

Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad related from Abu Juhayfah, from Abdullah [ibn Mas'ud]: "There is no year that is more abundant in rain than another year, but Allah distributes it wherever He wills: one year here and another year there." Then he recited: ﴿And there is nothing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We do not send it down except in a known measure.﴾ Narrated by Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari].

He also said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Hasan narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Salim informed us, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, concerning His words: ﴿And We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾. He said: "No year is more abundant in rain than another year, nor less, but He sends rain upon one people and deprives others, and it may fall in the sea." He said: "It has reached us that with the rain there descend angels more numerous than the offspring of Iblis and the offspring of Adam, who count every drop wherever it falls and whatever it causes to grow."[1]

Al-Bazzar said: Dawud, who is Ibn Bakr al-Tustari, narrated to us; Hayyan ibn Aghlab ibn Tamim narrated to us; my father narrated to me, from Hisham, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The treasuries of Allah are speech. Then [al-Bazzar] said: "No one narrates it except Aghlab, and he was not strong. Many of the earlier scholars narrated from him, and only his son narrated it from him."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾, meaning they fertilize the clouds so that they pour forth water, and they fertilize the trees so that they burst forth with their leaves and blossoms.

He mentioned these as "winds" in the plural form, so that fertilization may come from them, in contrast to the barren wind, which He mentioned in the singular and described as barren, meaning without fertilization, because fertilization occurs only between two things or more.

Al-A'mash related from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Qays ibn al-Sakan, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, concerning His words: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾, that he said: "The winds are sent, and they carry water from the sky, then they stir the clouds until they pour forth, just as a she-camel in heat [or a fertile animal] discharges."

Ibn Abbas, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Qatadah said likewise.

Al-Dahhak said: Allah sends them upon the clouds, and they fertilize them, and so they become filled with water.

Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi said: Allah sends the "bringers of good tidings" (al-mubashshirah), and they scatter the earth [with rain], then Allah sends the "stirrers" (al-muthirah), which stir up the clouds, then Allah sends the "gatherers" (al-mu'allifah), which gather the clouds, then Allah sends the fertilizing winds (al-lawaqih), which fertilize the trees. Then he recited: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing.﴾

Ibn Jarir has also related, through the report of Ubays ibn Maymun, from Abu al-Muhazzim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The south wind is from Paradise, and it is the fertilizing wind (al-rih al-lawaqih) that Allah mentioned in His Book, and in it there are benefits for people." This is a weak chain of narration.

Imam Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi said in his Musnad: Sufyan narrated to us, Amr ibn Dinar narrated to us, Yazid ibn Ju'dubah al-Laythi informed me that he heard Abdullah ibn Mikhraq narrate from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah created in Paradise a wind after the [other] wind by seven years. Beyond it is a closed door, and the wind comes to you only through that door. If it were opened, it would scatter everything between the heaven and the earth. It is called al-Azyab with Allah, and among you it is the south wind."[3]

* *

As for His words: ﴿So We gave you to drink from it﴾, meaning: We sent it down to you as sweet water from which you can drink. And had We willed, We would have made it salty and bitter, as Allah points out in another verse in Surah al-Waqi'ah, which is His words: ﴿Have you considered the water which you drink? Is it you who bring it down from the cloud, or are We the ones who bring it down? If We willed, We would make it bitter. Then why do you not give thanks?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:68-70]. And in His words: ﴿It is He who sends down water from the sky; from it is drink, and from it are trees in which you pasture [your livestock]﴾ [al-Naml 27:10].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And you are not its keepers﴾, Sufyan al-Thawri said: "Withholders."

It may also be that the intended meaning is: "And you are not its guardians. Rather, We send it down and We preserve it for you, and We make it flow as springs and streams in the earth. Had Allah willed, He would have made it sink away and taken it. But out of His mercy, He sent it down, made it sweet, and preserved it in springs, wells, rivers and elsewhere, so that it remains for them throughout the year, to drink from and to water their livestock, crops and fruit trees."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death﴾, this is an informing about His power over the origination of creation and its return, and that it is He who brought creation into being from nothing, then causes them to die, then resurrects them all for the Day of Assembly.

He also informed that He, exalted is He, inherits the earth and whoever is upon it, and to Him they will return.

Then He said, informing about the completeness of His knowledge of them, the first of them and the last of them: ﴿We certainly know those among you who go before, and We certainly know those who come later.﴾

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "Those who go before" are everyone who has perished from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, and "those who come later" are those who are alive and those who will come until the Day of Resurrection.

Similar was related from Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Sha'bi and others. This is also the opinion chosen by Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him.[4]

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from a man, from Marwan ibn al-Hakam, that he said: "Some people used to hang back in the rows because of the women, so Allah revealed: ﴿We certainly know those among you who go before, and We certainly know those who come later.﴾"[5]

A very strange hadith has also been reported regarding this. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi narrated to me, Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, Amr ibn Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "A woman used to pray behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ibn Abbas said: 'No, by Allah, I have never seen anyone like her.' Some of the Muslims, when they prayed, would move forward (to avoid seeing her), and some would hang back, and when they prostrated, they would look at her from beneath their armpits!! So Allah revealed: ﴿We certainly know those among you who go before, and We certainly know those who come later.﴾"

Similarly, Ahmad and Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir related it, and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in the Book of Tafsir of their Sunan, and Ibn Majah, through various chains from Nuh ibn Qays al-Hudani.[6] Ahmad, Abu Dawud and others declared him trustworthy, and it is related from Ibn Ma'in that he weakened him. Muslim and the authors of the Sunan took narrations from him.

This hadith has severe irregularity (nakarah). It was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from Amr ibn Malik, who is al-Nukri, that he heard Abu al-Jawza' say concerning His words: ﴿We certainly know those among you who go before﴾, "in the rows in prayer," and ﴿those who come later﴾. So the apparent view is that this is only the statement of Abu al-Jawza', with no mention of Ibn Abbas in it.[7] al-Tirmidhi said: "This is more likely than the narration of Nuh ibn Qays." And Allah knows best.

Thus Ibn Jarir also related from Muhammad ibn Abi Ma'shar, from his father, that he heard Awn ibn Abdullah discussing with Muhammad ibn Ka'b His words: ﴿We certainly know those among you who go before, and We certainly know those who come later﴾, and that they refer to the rows of prayer. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "It is not so. ﴿We certainly know those among you who go before﴾ refers to the dead and the slain, and ﴿those who come later﴾ refers to those who have yet to be created. ﴿And indeed your Lord will gather them; indeed He is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾." Awn ibn Abdullah said: "May Allah grant you success and reward you with good."[8]

Allah, exalted is He, mentions His elevating Adam among His angels before creating him, and His honouring him by commanding the angels to prostrate to him. He also mentions the refusal of Iblis, his enemy, to prostrate to him, unlike all the other angels, out of envy, disbelief, obstinacy, arrogance, and boasting falsely. For this reason He said: ﴿I would not prostrate to a human whom You created from clay, from black mud altered and moulded.﴾ As He said in another verse: ﴿I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 12] And his saying [[In T and A: "And He said in the other verse."]] ﴿Tell me, is this the one whom You have honoured above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few.﴾ [Al-Isra': 62]

Ibn Jarir has narrated here a strange and remarkable report (athar) from the narration of Shabib ibn Bishr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Allah created the angels, He said: "I am creating a human from clay. When I have fashioned him, prostrate to him." They said: "We will not do that." So He sent a fire upon them and it burned them. Then He created other angels and said to them the same thing, and they said: "We will not do that." So He sent a fire upon them and it burned them. Then He created other angels and said: "I am creating a human from clay. When I have created him, prostrate to him," and they refused, so He sent a fire upon them and it burned them. Then He created angels and said: "I am creating a human from clay. When I have created him, prostrate to him." [[Supplement from T, A, and al-Tabari.]] They said: "We hear and we obey," except Iblis, who was among the first disbelievers. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/22).]]

As for the authenticity of this report from him, it is far-fetched, and the apparent view is that it is an Isra'iliyyat (a narration of Israelite origin), and Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 15, verses 39–44:

Allah the Exalted says, reporting about Iblis, his rebelliousness and his arrogance, that he said to the Lord: ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾. Some of them said: he swore by Allah's leading him astray.

I say: It is also possible that it means: because You led me astray and misguided me. ﴿I will certainly make [evil] seem attractive to them﴾, that is, to the descendants of Adam, peace be upon him, ﴿on earth﴾, that is, I will make sins beloved to them, encourage them towards them, incite them to them, and provoke them greatly. ﴿And I will surely mislead them all﴾, that is, just as You misled me, and I will persist in that. ﴿Except for Your sincere servants among them﴾, as he said: ﴿Have you considered this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few﴾ [Al-Isra: 62].

Allah the Exalted said to him, threatening and warning him: ﴿This is a straight path to Me﴾, that is, your return, all of you, is to Me, and I will recompense you for your deeds: if [they are] good, then [the recompense is] good, and if [they are] evil, then [the recompense is] evil, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [Al-Fajr: 14].

It has also been said: the path of truth leads back to Allah the Exalted and ends at Him. This was said by Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah, as He said: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the path﴾ [An-Nahl: 9].

Qays ibn 'Abbad, Muhammad ibn Sirin and Qatadah recited: "This is a path, ʿAliyyun (exalted), straight," like His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 4], meaning elevated. The well-known recitation (qira'ah) is the first one.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾, that is, those for whom I have decreed guidance; there is no way for you over them and no access for you to them. ﴿Except those who follow you among the deviators﴾. This is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati', an exception that is not of the same kind as what precedes it).

Ibn Jarir has transmitted here, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Mawhab, who narrated to us from Yazid ibn Qusayt, who said: The prophets used to have places of worship outside their settlements. When a prophet wished to seek information from his Lord about something, he would go out to his place of worship, pray what Allah had decreed for him, and then ask what he wished. While a prophet was in his place of worship, the enemy of Allah, meaning Iblis, came and sat between him and the qiblah. The Prophet said: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan." [The enemy of Allah said: "Have you considered the one you seek refuge from? He is right here." The Prophet said: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan."] [[Addition from manuscripts T and A, and al-Tabari.]] He said: He repeated that three times. The enemy of Allah said: "Tell me, by what means do you escape me?" The Prophet said: "Rather, tell me, by what means do you overcome the son of Adam?" He said it twice, and each of them took hold of the other. The Prophet said: "Indeed Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you among the deviators﴾." The enemy of Allah said: "I heard this before you were born." The Prophet said: "And Allah says: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Shaytan provokes you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing﴾ [Al-A'raf: 200]." "And I swear by Allah," [he said], "I have never sensed you except that I sought refuge in Allah from you." The enemy of Allah said: "You have spoken the truth. By this you escape from me." The Prophet said: "Tell me, by what means do you overcome the son of Adam?" He said: "I seize him at times of anger and desire."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/24).]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all﴾, that is, Hell is the promised place of all who followed Iblis, just as He said about the Qur'an: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, then the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

Then He informed that Hell has seven gates: ﴿For each gate of them is a portion designated﴾. It has also been said: the path of truth leads back to Allah the Exalted and ends at Him. This was said by Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah, as He said: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the path﴾ [An-Nahl: 9].

Qays ibn 'Abbad, Muhammad ibn Sirin and Qatadah recited: "This is a path, ʿAliyyun (exalted), straight," like His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 4], meaning elevated. The well-known recitation (qira'ah) is the first one.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾, that is, those for whom I have decreed guidance; there is no way for you over them and no access for you to them. ﴿Except those who follow you among the deviators﴾. This is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati', an exception that is not of the same kind as what precedes it).

Ibn Jarir has transmitted here, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Mawhab, who narrated to us from Yazid ibn Qusayt, who said: The prophets used to have places of worship outside their settlements. When a prophet wished to seek information from his Lord about something, he would go out to his place of worship, pray what Allah had decreed for him, and then ask what he wished. While a prophet was in his place of worship, the enemy of Allah, meaning Iblis, came and sat between him and the qiblah. The Prophet said: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan." [The enemy of Allah said: "Have you considered the one you seek refuge from? He is right here." The Prophet said: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan."] [[Addition from manuscripts T and A, and al-Tabari.]] He said: He repeated that three times. The enemy of Allah said: "Tell me, by what means do you escape me?" The Prophet said: "Rather, tell me, by what means do you overcome the son of Adam?" He said it twice, and each of them took hold of the other. The Prophet said: "Indeed Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you among the deviators﴾." The enemy of Allah said: "I heard this before you were born." The Prophet said: "And Allah says: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Shaytan provokes you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing﴾ [Al-A'raf: 200]." "And I swear by Allah," [he said], "I have never sensed you except that I sought refuge in Allah from you." The enemy of Allah said: "You have spoken the truth. By this you escape from me." The Prophet said: "Tell me, by what means do you overcome the son of Adam?" He said: "I seize him at times of anger and desire."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/24).]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all﴾, that is, Hell is the promised place of all who followed Iblis, just as He said about the Qur'an: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, then the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

Then He informed that Hell has seven gates: ﴿For each gate of them is a portion designated﴾. That is, a portion of Iblis's followers has been decreed for each gate of it, to enter it, with no escape for them from it. May Allah protect us from it. Each one enters through a gate according to his deeds, and settles in a level according to his actions.

Isma'il ibn Ulayyah and Shu'bah both said, from Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, from Hittan ibn Abdullah, that he said: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was delivering a sermon, say: "Indeed, the gates of Hell are like this," [Abu Harun said: "layers, some above others"] [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/24).]].

Isra'il narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Hubayrah ibn Yurim, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The gates of Hell are seven, some above others. The first fills up, then the second, then the third, until they are all filled."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/24).]]

Ikrimah said: ﴿Seven gates﴾ means seven layers.

Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Seven gates﴾: the first of them is Jahannam, then Laza, then Hutamah, then Sa'ir, then Saqar, then Jahim, then Hawiyah.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas something similar. Likewise, it is also reported from al-A'mash in similar terms.

Qatadah said: ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate of them is a portion designated﴾. By Allah, they are dwelling places according to their deeds. Ibn Jarir transmitted these.

Juwaybir said, from al-Dahhak: ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate of them is a portion designated﴾. He said: One gate is for the Jews, one gate for the Christians, one gate for the Sabians, one gate for the Magians, one gate for those who associated partners [with Allah], meaning the disbelieving Arabs, one gate for the hypocrites, and one gate for the people of monotheism. The people of monotheism are hoped for, but those others are never hoped for.

At-Tirmidhi said: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Junayd, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Hell has seven gates: one gate of them is for those who draw the sword against my ummah," or he said, "against the ummah of Muhammad."

Then he said: "We do not know it except from the hadith of Malik ibn Mighwal."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3123), where he said: "This is a gharib hadith, we do not know it except from the hadith of Malik ibn Mighwal."]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Khallal narrated to us, Zayd, meaning Ibn Yahya, narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Nadrah, from Samurah ibn Jundub, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying: ﴿For each gate of them is a portion designated﴾, he said: "Among the people of the Fire are those whom the Fire seizes up to their ankles, and among them are those whom the Fire seizes up to their waists, and among them are those whom the Fire seizes up to their collarbones, according to their deeds. That is His saying: ﴿For each gate of them is a portion designated﴾."[[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/82) at length. The original hadith is in Sahih Muslim, no. (2845), without mention of the verse, up to his words: "the Fire seizes him up to his waist."]]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 15, verses 39–44:

Allah the Exalted says, reporting about Iblis, his rebelliousness and his arrogance, that he said to the Lord: ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾. Some of them said: he swore by Allah's leading him astray.

I say: It is also possible that it means: because You led me astray and misguided me. ﴿I will certainly make [evil] seem attractive to them﴾, that is, to the descendants of Adam, peace be upon him, ﴿on earth﴾, that is, I will make sins beloved to them, encourage them towards them, incite them to them, and provoke them greatly. ﴿And I will surely mislead them all﴾, that is, just as You misled me, and I will persist in that. ﴿Except for Your sincere servants among them﴾, as he said: ﴿Have you considered this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few﴾ [Al-Isra: 62].

Allah the Exalted said to him, threatening and warning him: ﴿This is a straight path to Me﴾, that is, your return, all of you, is to Me, and I will recompense you for your deeds: if [they are] good, then [the recompense is] good, and if [they are] evil, then [the recompense is] evil, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [Al-Fajr: 14].

It has also been said: the path of truth leads back to Allah the Exalted and ends at Him. This was said by Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah, as He said: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the path﴾ [An-Nahl: 9].

Qays ibn 'Abbad, Muhammad ibn Sirin and Qatadah recited: "This is a path, ʿAliyyun (exalted), straight," like His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 4], meaning elevated. The well-known recitation (qira'ah) is the first one.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾, that is, those for whom I have decreed guidance; there is no way for you over them and no access for you to them. ﴿Except those who follow you among the deviators﴾. This is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati', an exception that is not of the same kind as what precedes it).

Ibn Jarir has transmitted here, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Mawhab, who narrated to us from Yazid ibn Qusayt, who said: The prophets used to have places of worship outside their settlements. When a prophet wished to seek information from his Lord about something, he would go out to his place of worship, pray what Allah had decreed for him, and then ask what he wished. While a prophet was in his place of worship, the enemy of Allah, meaning Iblis, came and sat between him and the qiblah. The Prophet said: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan." [The enemy of Allah said: "Have you considered the one you seek refuge from? He is right here." The Prophet said: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan."] [[Addition from manuscripts T and A, and al-Tabari.]] He said: He repeated that three times. The enemy of Allah said: "Tell me, by what means do you escape me?" The Prophet said: "Rather, tell me, by what means do you overcome the son of Adam?" He said it twice, and each of them took hold of the other. The Prophet said: "Indeed Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you among the deviators﴾." The enemy of Allah said: "I heard this before you were born." The Prophet said: "And Allah says: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Shaytan provokes you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing﴾ [Al-A'raf: 200]." "And I swear by Allah," [he said], "I have never sensed you except that I sought refuge in Allah from you." The enemy of Allah said: "You have spoken the truth. By this you escape from me." The Prophet said: "Tell me, by what means do you overcome the son of Adam?" He said: "I seize him at times of anger and desire."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/24).]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all﴾, that is, Hell is the promised place of all who followed Iblis, just as He said about the Qur'an: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, then the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

Then He informed that Hell has seven gates: ﴿For each gate of them is a portion designated﴾. That is, a portion of Iblis's followers has been decreed for each gate of it, to enter it, with no escape for them from it. May Allah protect us from it. Each one enters through a gate according to his deeds, and settles in a level according to his actions.

Isma'il ibn Ulayyah and Shu'bah both said, from Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, from Hittan ibn Abdullah, that he said: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was delivering a sermon, say: "Indeed, the gates of Hell are like this," [Abu Harun said: "layers, some above others"] [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/24).]].

Isra'il narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Hubayrah ibn Yurim, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The gates of Hell are seven, some above others. The first fills up, then the second, then the third, until they are all filled."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/24).]]

Ikrimah said: ﴿Seven gates﴾ means seven layers.

Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Seven gates﴾: the first of them is Jahannam, then Laza, then Hutamah, then Sa'ir, then Saqar, then Jahim, then Hawiyah.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas something similar. Likewise, it is also reported from al-A'mash in similar terms.

Qatadah said: ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate of them is a portion designated﴾. By Allah, they are dwelling places according to their deeds. Ibn Jarir transmitted these.

Juwaybir said, from al-Dahhak: ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate of them is a portion designated﴾. He said: One gate is for the Jews, one gate for the Christians, one gate for the Sabians, one gate for the Magians, one gate for those who associated partners [with Allah], meaning the disbelieving Arabs, one gate for the hypocrites, and one gate for the people of monotheism. The people of monotheism are hoped for, but those others are never hoped for.

At-Tirmidhi said: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Junayd, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Hell has seven gates: one gate of them is for those who draw the sword against my ummah," or he said, "against the ummah of Muhammad."

Then he said: "We do not know it except from the hadith of Malik ibn Mighwal."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3123), where he said: "This is a gharib hadith, we do not know it except from the hadith of Malik ibn Mighwal."]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Khallal narrated to us, Zayd, meaning Ibn Yahya, narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Nadrah, from Samurah ibn Jundub, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His saying: ﴿For each gate of them is a portion designated﴾, he said: "Among the people of the Fire are those whom the Fire seizes up to their ankles, and among them are those whom the Fire seizes up to their waists, and among them are those whom the Fire seizes up to their collarbones, according to their deeds. That is His saying: ﴿For each gate of them is a portion designated﴾."[[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/82) at length. The original hadith is in Sahih Muslim, no. (2845), without mention of the verse, up to his words: "the Fire seizes him up to his waist."]]

When Allah mentioned the condition of the people of the Fire, He followed it with a mention of the people of Paradise, and that they are in gardens and springs.

* *

His saying: ﴿Enter it in peace﴾ means: safe from calamities, with greetings of peace upon you, ﴿secure﴾ from every fear and terror, and do not fear expulsion, cessation, or extinction.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, [and they will be] brothers, on couches facing one another﴾. Al-Qasim narrated from Abu Umamah, who said: The people of Paradise will enter Paradise carrying the rancor and enmity that were in their hearts in this world. When they meet and face one another, Allah will remove from their hearts whatever resentment was in them in the world. Then he recited: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/25) through the chain of Israʾil, from Bishr al-Basri, from al-Qasim, with the same wording.]]

In this narration it is as stated. Al-Qasim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, in his narration from Abu Umamah, is weak (ḍaʿīf).

Sunayd also narrated in his tafsir: Ibn Fudalah related to us, from Luqman, from Abu Umamah, who said: No believer will enter Paradise until Allah removes whatever resentment is in their breasts, until He removes from him something like the bite of a predatory beast.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/25).]]

This agrees with what is in the Sahih, from the narration of Qatadah, who said: Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji related to us that Abu Saʿid al-Khudri told them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The believers will be delivered from the Fire, and they will be held back on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and retribution will be exacted from some of them against others for the injustices that existed between them in the world. When they have been purified and cleansed, permission will be given to them to enter Paradise."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6535).]]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Hasan related to us, Yazid ibn Harun related to us, Hisham informed us, from Muhammad, that is Ibn Sirin, who said: al-Ashtar asked permission to enter upon ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, while a son of Talhah was with him. ʿAli detained him, then gave him permission. When he entered, he said: "I see that you only held me back for this?" He said: "Indeed." He said: "I think that if a son of ʿUthman were with you, you would have held me back as well?" He said: "Indeed. I hope that I and ʿUthman will be among those of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts [brothers] on couches facing one another﴾."[[The word "brothers" in brackets is an addition from manuscript T.]][[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/26).]]

And al-Hasan related to us: Abu Muʿawiyah al-Darir related to us, Abu Malik al-Ashjaʿi related to us, from Abu Habibah, a freedman of Talhah, who said: ʿImran ibn Talhah entered upon ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, after he had finished with the people of the Camel. He welcomed him and said: "I hope that Allah will make me and your father among those about whom Allah said: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, [and they will be] brothers, on couches facing one another﴾." He said: Two men were sitting at the edge of the carpet, and they said: "Allah is more just than that! You kill them yesterday, and you will be brothers!" ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Be off, [you are] the most distant and the most remote of lands! Then who would they be if not I and Talhah?" And Abu Muʿawiyah mentioned the hadith in full.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/25).]]

Waki narrated from Aban ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Bajali, from Nuʿaym ibn Abi Hind, from Ribʿi ibn Khirash, from ʿAli, similar to it, and in it he said: A man from Hamdan stood up and said: "Allah is more just than that, O Commander of the Faithful!" He said: ʿAli shouted at him with a great cry, so that I thought the palace would collapse from it. Then he said: "If it is not us, then who is it?"[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/25) through the chain of Waki.]]

Saʿid ibn Masruq said, from Abu Talhah, and he mentioned it, in which: al-Harith al-Aʿwar said that, so ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, stood up to him and struck him on the head with something that was in his hand, and said: "Then who are they, O one-eyed man, if it is not us?"

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: Ibn Jurmuz, the slayer of al-Zubayr, came asking permission to enter upon ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, and he kept him waiting a long time, then gave him permission. He said to him: "As for the people of trials, you turn away from them." ʿAli said: "May dust be in your mouth! I hope that I, Talhah, and al-Zubayr are among those about whom Allah said: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, [and they will be] brothers, on couches facing one another﴾."

Similarly, al-Thawri narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from ʿAli, something similar.

Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah said, from Israʾil, from Abu Musa, who heard al-Hasan al-Basri say: ʿAli said: "By Allah, concerning us, the people of Badr, this verse was revealed: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, [and they will be] brothers, on couches facing one another﴾."

Kathir al-Nawaʾ said: I entered upon Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli and said: "My ally is your ally, my peace is your peace, my enemy is your enemy, and my war is your war. I ask you by Allah: do you disassociate yourself from Abu Bakr and ʿUmar?" He said: ﴿Then indeed I would have gone astray, and I would not be among the guided﴾ [al-Anʿam: 56]. "Befriend both of them, O Kathir, and whatever you attain, it is upon my neck." Then he recited this verse: ﴿[brothers] on couches facing one another﴾ and said: Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with them all.[[The word in T is "bardahuma" and in A "bardaha", meaning "disassociate from them".]]

Al-Thawri said, from a man, from Abu Salih, concerning His saying: ﴿[brothers] on couches facing one another﴾: They are ten: Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthman, ʿAli, Talhah, al-Zubayr, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, Saʿid ibn Zayd, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with them all.

* *

His saying: ﴿facing one another﴾. Mujahid said: Some of them do not look at the back of the neck of others.

There is also a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) hadith concerning it. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Yahya ibn ʿAbdak al-Qazwini related to us, Hassan ibn Hassan related to us, Ibrahim ibn Bishr related to us, Yahya ibn Maʿin related to us, from Ibrahim al-Qurashi, from Saʿid ibn Shurahbil, from Zayd ibn Abi Awfa, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and recited this verse: ﴿[brothers] on couches facing one another﴾, [meaning] for the sake of Allah, looking at one another.[[Al-Bukhari also narrated it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (3/386) in the biography of Zayd ibn Abi Awfa, through the chain of Hassan ibn Hassan, and said: "It has no follower (la yutaba ʿalayh)."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿No fatigue will touch them therein﴾ means: hardship and harm, as has come in the Two Sahihs: "Indeed Allah commanded me to give glad tidings to Khadijah of a house in Paradise made of pearls, in which there is no noise and no fatigue."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3820) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2432), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And they will not be removed from it﴾, as has come in the hadith: "It will be said: O people of Paradise, indeed for you is that you will be healthy and never fall ill; and indeed for you is that you will live and never die; and indeed for you is that you will be young and never grow old; and indeed for you is that you will dwell and never depart." And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Abiding therein forever, they will not desire any change from it﴾ [al-Kahf: 108].

* *

His saying: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ means: Tell them, O Muhammad, that My servants, that I am full of mercy and full of painful punishment.

The like of this noble verse has already been mentioned, and it indicates the two stations of hope and fear. Concerning the cause of its revelation, Musa ibn ʿUbaydah narrated from Mus‘ab ibn Thabit, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by some of his companions who were laughing, and he said: "Remember Paradise, and remember the Fire." Then this was revealed: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, and it is mursal (a report whose chain omits a companion), and Musa ibn ʿUbaydah al-Rabadhi is weak.[[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/86), attributing it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna related to me, Ishaq related to us, Ibn al-Makki informed us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Mus‘ab ibn Thabit informed us, ʿAsim ibn ʿUbayd Allah related to us, from Ibn Abi Rabah, from a man from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appeared to us from the gate through which the Banu Shaybah enter, and said: "Do I not see you laughing?" Then he turned away, and when he reached al-Hajar he came back to us backwards, and said: "When I went out, Jibril, peace be upon him, came and said: O Muhammad, indeed Allah says: Why do you make My servants despair? ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/27).]]

Saʿid said, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾: It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If the servant knew the extent of Allah's pardon, he would not refrain from what is forbidden; and if he knew the extent of His punishment, he would destroy himself."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/27) and by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Husn al-Zann billah, no. (64), through the chain of Saʿid from Qatadah as a mursal report. A similar report is narrated with a continuous chain from Ibn ʿUmar and Abu Saʿid al-Khudri. As for the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Husn al-Zann billah, no. (63), through Musa from ʿAtiyyah, from Ibn ʿUmar, as a marfuʿ report: "If you knew the extent of the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, you would not rely on your deeds, and if you knew the extent of His anger, nothing would benefit you." As for the hadith of Abu Saʿid, al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, and its wording is: "If you knew the extent of the mercy of Allah, you would not rely [on it]—I think he said: upon it." Al-Haythami said in al-Majmaʿ (10/384): "Its chain is hasan (good)."]]

When Allah mentioned the condition of the people of the Fire, He followed it with a mention of the people of Paradise, and that they are in gardens and springs.

* *

His saying: ﴿Enter it in peace﴾ means: safe from calamities, with greetings of peace upon you, ﴿secure﴾ from every fear and terror, and do not fear expulsion, cessation, or extinction.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, [and they will be] brothers, on couches facing one another﴾. Al-Qasim narrated from Abu Umamah, who said: The people of Paradise will enter Paradise carrying the rancor and enmity that were in their hearts in this world. When they meet and face one another, Allah will remove from their hearts whatever resentment was in them in the world. Then he recited: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/25) through the chain of Israʾil, from Bishr al-Basri, from al-Qasim, with the same wording.]]

In this narration it is as stated. Al-Qasim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, in his narration from Abu Umamah, is weak (ḍaʿīf).

Sunayd also narrated in his tafsir: Ibn Fudalah related to us, from Luqman, from Abu Umamah, who said: No believer will enter Paradise until Allah removes whatever resentment is in their breasts, until He removes from him something like the bite of a predatory beast.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/25).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, and it is mursal (a report whose chain omits a companion), and Musa ibn ʿUbaydah al-Rabadhi is weak.[[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/86), attributing it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna related to me, Ishaq related to us, Ibn al-Makki informed us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Mus‘ab ibn Thabit informed us, ʿAsim ibn ʿUbayd Allah related to us, from Ibn Abi Rabah, from a man from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appeared to us from the gate through which the Banu Shaybah enter, and said: "Do I not see you laughing?" Then he turned away, and when he reached al-Hajar he came back to us backwards, and said: "When I went out, Jibril, peace be upon him, came and said: O Muhammad, indeed Allah says: Why do you make My servants despair? ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/27).]]

Saʿid said, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾: It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If the servant knew the extent of Allah's pardon, he would not refrain from what is forbidden; and if he knew the extent of His punishment, he would destroy himself."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/27) and by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Husn al-Zann billah, no. (64), through the chain of Saʿid from Qatadah as a mursal report. A similar report is narrated with a continuous chain from Ibn ʿUmar and Abu Saʿid al-Khudri. As for the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Husn al-Zann billah, no. (63), through Musa from ʿAtiyyah, from Ibn ʿUmar, as a marfuʿ report: "If you knew the extent of the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, you would not rely on your deeds, and if you knew the extent of His anger, nothing would benefit you." As for the hadith of Abu Saʿid, al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, and its wording is: "If you knew the extent of the mercy of Allah, you would not rely [on it]—I think he said: upon it." Al-Haythami said in al-Majmaʿ (10/384): "Its chain is hasan (good)."]]

Ibn Kathir says: Allah, exalted is He, says: "And inform them, O Muhammad, of the story of the guests of Ibrahim (﴿ضَيْفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾)." The word "ḍayf" (guest) is used for one or many, like "zawr" and "sufr." "When they entered upon him and said, 'Peace,' he said, 'Indeed, we are fearful of you'" (﴿قَالَ إِنَّا مِنْكُمْ وَجِلُونَ﴾), meaning: afraid.

He mentioned the reason for his fear of them: when he saw that their hands did not reach the food he had brought near for them as hospitality, which was the fat roasted calf (al-'ijl al-samin al-ḥanidh).

﴿They said, "Do not be afraid."﴾ That is: do not fear. ﴿And they gave him the good news of a knowledgeable boy﴾ (Adh-Dhariyat: 28), who is Ishaq (peace be upon him), as was mentioned in Surah Hud.

Then he said, amazed at his old age and the old age of his wife, and seeking certainty about the promise: ﴿"Do you give me good news although old age has touched me? Then what is it you give good news of?"﴾ They answered him, emphasizing what they had given him as good news, confirming it and giving glad tidings after glad tidings: ﴿"We have given you the truth, so do not be among the despairing."﴾ Some of them read it as "al-qanitin" (al-muqnitin). He answered them that he does not despair, but he hopes from Allah for a child, even though he has grown old and his wife has aged, for he knows from Allah's power and mercy what is greater than that.

Ibn Kathir said, concerning Lut (Lot) when the angels came to him in the form of handsome young men, and they entered his house: he said, ﴿Indeed, you are a people unknown (to me).﴾ They said, ﴿Rather, we have come to you with that about which they used to doubt,﴾ meaning: with their punishment, their destruction and their annihilation, which they used to doubt would befall them and descend upon their courtyard. ﴿And We have brought you the truth,﴾ as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth﴾ [al-Hijr: 8].

* *

His saying, ﴿And indeed, We are truthful,﴾ is an affirmation of their report to him (in the text of one manuscript: "bikhabarihim") with what they had told him, of his salvation and the destruction of his people. [And Allah knows best.]

Ibn Kathir said: Allah mentions that the angels commanded Lut, peace be upon him, to travel with his family after a portion of the night had passed, and that Lut should walk behind them so that he could better guard them.

Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to walk at the rear (saaqah) during the military expeditions, urging on the weak and carrying the one who had fallen behind.[[In manuscript T: "in the expedition, indeed it was," and in manuscript A: "in the expedition, and indeed it would be."]][[Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan, no. 2639, from the hadith of Jabir, and its wording is: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to lag behind on the march, urging on the weak, providing mounts, and supplicating for them."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And let none of you look back,﴾ meaning: when you hear the cry against the people, do not turn to them, but leave them to the punishment and torment that has befallen them. ﴿And proceed where you are commanded,﴾ as if there were with them someone guiding them on the way.

﴿And We decreed this matter to him,﴾ meaning: We conveyed this to him in advance, ﴿that the last remnant of these people would be cut off by morning.﴾ Meaning: at the time of dawn, as He said in another verse: ﴿Indeed, their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?﴾ [Hud: 81]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 15, verses 67–72:

He, exalted is He, informs about the coming of the people of Lut (Lot) when they learned of his guests and the beauty of their faces, and that they came rejoicing and joyful over them: ﴿He said, "Indeed, these are my guests, so do not disgrace me. And fear Allah and do not humiliate me."﴾

This he said to them before he knew that they were messengers of Allah, as He said in the context of Surah Hud. Here, however, the mention that they were messengers of Allah came first, and it is joined (by the conjunction "wa") to the mention of his people's coming and his arguing with them. But the particle "wa" (and) does not require sequence, especially when evidence indicates otherwise. So they replied to him: ﴿Did we not forbid you from (dealing with) the worlds?﴾ That is: "Did we not forbid you to host anyone?" So he directed them to their wives, and what their Lord had created for them of lawful private parts. The discussion of this has already been presented earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary.

All of this occurred while they were heedless of what was intended for them, and of the calamity that had surrounded them, and of the lasting punishment that would overtake them at dawn. For this reason, the Exalted said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿By your life, indeed they were wandering blindly in their intoxication.﴾ He, exalted is He, swore by the life of His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and in this there is great honor, a lofty station and a wide dignity.

ʿAmr ibn Malik al-Nukri narrated from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he said: "Allah did not create, nor scatter, nor bring into being, a soul more honored by Him than Muhammad ﷺ, and I have not heard that Allah swore by the life of anyone other than him." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿By your life, indeed they were wandering blindly in their intoxication.﴾ [That is: "By your life, your lifespan, and your remaining in the world, indeed they were wandering blindly in their intoxication."] Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Qatadah said: ﴿in their intoxication﴾ means in their misguidance, and ﴿wandering blindly﴾ means playing about.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿By your life﴾ means by your living, ﴿indeed they were wandering blindly in their intoxication﴾ — he said: they are bewildered.

His saying: ﴿And indeed it is on an established road⁠﴾ means: the town of Sodom, which was struck by what struck it of overturning, both material and figurative, and the casting of stones, until it became a foul, wicked lake, while the road past it—whose paths are open and well-traveled—remains continuous until today. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning and at night. Will you not then reason?⁠﴾ [al-Saffat: 137–138].

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers⁠﴾ means: what We did to the people of Lut of destruction and annihilation, and Our saving of Lut and his family, is truly a clear and manifest proof for the believers in Allah and His messengers.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿So the Cry seized them﴾, which was the thundering sound that came upon them at the rising of the sun, that is, its emergence. This occurred along with the lifting of their towns up to the heights of the sky, then their overturning, making their highest part their lowest, and the sending down upon them of stones of sijjil (hard baked clay). The discussion of sijjil has already been given in Surat Hud, sufficiently.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern⁠﴾ means: the traces of these punishments are clearly visible upon those lands to whoever reflects on them and discerns them with the eye of his sight and his insight, as Mujahid said concerning His words ﴿for those who discern⁠﴾: "They are those who look closely (al-mutafarrisin)."

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern⁠﴾.

It was related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mula'i. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3127) and Tafsir al-Tabari (14/31).] Al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know it except through this route."

Ibn Jarir also said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to me, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, al-Furat ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, Maymun ibn Mihran narrated to us, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the firasah of the believer, for the believer looks with the light of Allah." Companions of the Thicket (al-Aykah): they were the people of Shu'ayb.

Al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others said: al-Aykah means dense, intertwined trees.

Their wrongdoing was their associating partners with Allah, their highway robbery, and their short-changing in measure and weight. So Allah took vengeance on them through the Blast (al-Sayhah), the Quake (al-Rajfah), and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy (Yawm al-Zullah), and they were close to the people of Lut in time, after them, and neighbours to them in place. Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed, they were on a clear highway﴾, meaning, a clear road.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: a clear road, evident. Therefore, when Shu'ayb warned his people, he said in his warning to them: ﴿And the people of Lut are not far from you﴾.

The companions of the Rock (Al-Hijr) are Thamud, the people who denied their prophet Salih. Whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers. For this reason, the denial of the messengers is attributed to them.

He, may He be exalted, mentions that He gave them signs that proved the truth of what Salih brought them. Among these was the she-camel that Allah brought forth for them from a solid rock in answer to Salih's supplication. She used to graze in their land, and she had her share of water, while they had their share on a known day. When they transgressed and hamstrung her, he said to them: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied﴾ [Hud: 65]. He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17].

He, may He be exalted, mentions that they ﴿used to carve out homes from the mountains, feeling secure﴾, meaning without fear and without any need for them, but out of insolence, arrogance and frivolity. This is evident from their conduct in their houses in the Valley of Al-Hijr, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by on his way to Tabuk. He covered his head, urged on his mount, and said to his companions: "Do not enter the dwellings of the people who were punished, unless you are weeping; and if you cannot weep, then feign weeping, lest what befell them befall you." [This is from a hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (no. 3380) and by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 298), with the wording: "Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves..." and the hadith continues. Al-Bukhari also narrated it in his Sahih (no. 4702) with the wording: "Do not enter upon these people unless you are weeping; and if you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest there befall you the like of what befell them."]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So the Cry seized them at morning﴾, meaning at the time of morning on the fourth day. ﴿Then what they had earned did not avail them﴾, meaning the produce of their crops and fruits, which they hoarded and grudged the she-camel its water, until they hamstrung her so that she would not restrict their access to water. Those possessions did not repel anything from them, and did not benefit them when the command of your Lord came.
