Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 15, verses 87–88:

Allah, exalted is He, says to His Prophet: Just as We have given you the Mighty Qur'an, do not look at the worldly life and its adornments, nor at what We have given its people to enjoy, the fleeting splendour, in order to test them through it. Do not envy them for what they have, and do not let yourself be consumed with sorrow (ḥasarāt) over them because of their denial of you and their opposition to your religion. ﴿And lower your wing to the believers who follow you﴾ [Surah al-Shu'ara', 26:215], that is: be gentle and kind toward them, as Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and, toward the believers, kind and merciful﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah, 9:128].

Scholars have differed concerning the *al-Sab' al-Mathani* (the seven oft-repeated): what are they?

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and others said: They are the seven long surahs, meaning: al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf, and Yunus. This was stated explicitly by Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Sa'id said: In them Allah has explained the obligatory duties (fara'id), the prescribed punishments (hudud), the narratives (qasas), and the rulings (ahkam).

Ibn 'Abbas said: In them He has explained the parables (amthal), the reports (khabar), and the lessons (ibar).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi 'Umar told us, saying: Sufyan said: *al-Mathani* refers to: al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf, and al-Anfal and Bara'ah as one surah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: No one was given them except the Prophet ﷺ, and Musa was given two of them. This was narrated by Hushaym, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Walid ibn al-'Ayzar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from him.

Al-A'mash said, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was given seven of the long *mathani*, and Musa, peace be upon him, was given six. When he threw down the tablets, two were lifted and four remained.

Mujahid said: They are the seven long surahs. It is also said: They are the Mighty Qur'an.

Khasif said, from Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam, concerning the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: I have given you seven parts: commanding, forbidding, giving glad tidings, warning, striking parables, enumerating blessings, and informing you of the news of the Qur'an. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

The second view: they are al-Fatihah, which consists of seven verses. This was narrated from 'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, and Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn 'Abbas said: The basmalah is the seventh verse, and Allah has singled you out with it. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, Ibn Abi Mulaykah, Shahr ibn Hawshab, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Mujahid also held this view.

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that they are the Opening of the Book (Fatihat al-Kitab), and that they are repeated in every recitation. In another narration: in every obligatory or voluntary prayer unit (rak'ah).

Ibn Jarir chose this view and cited the hadiths related on this subject, which we mentioned earlier in the virtues of Surah al-Fatihah at the beginning of this tafsir, and to Allah belongs all praise.

Imam al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, cited two hadiths here:

The first: He said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, Ghundar told us, Shu'bah told us, from Khubayb ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn 'Asim, from Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla, who said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by me while I was praying, and he called me, but I did not come to him until I had finished praying. Then I came to him, and he said: "What prevented you from coming to me?" I said: I was praying. He said: "Did Allah not say: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you﴾ [Surah al-Anfal, 8:24]? Shall I not teach you the greatest surah in the Qur'an before I leave the mosque?" The Prophet ﷺ then started to leave, and I reminded him, and he said: "﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah, 1:2] is the seven oft-repeated and the Mighty Qur'an that I have been given." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4703.]

The second: He said: Adam told us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b told us, al-Maqburi told us, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Mother of the Qur'an is: the seven oft-repeated and the Mighty Qur'an." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4704.]

This is a clear text that al-Fatihah is the seven oft-repeated and the Mighty Qur'an. * *

As for His words: ﴿Do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to categories of them﴾ [Surah al-Hijr, 15:88], that is: be content with what Allah has given you of the Mighty Qur'an, and be independent of what they have of wealth and fleeting splendour.

From here Ibn 'Uyaynah interpreted the sound hadith: "He is not of us who does not chant the Qur'an melodiously" [see the earlier section on the virtues of the Qur'an, chapter: whoever does not chant the Qur'an] as meaning that one is made independent through it of anything else. This is a correct interpretation, but it is not the intended meaning of the hadith, as was mentioned earlier at the beginning of this tafsir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Waki' ibn al-Jarrah, who said: Musa ibn 'Ubaydah told us, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Rafi', companion of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The Prophet ﷺ hosted a guest, and the Prophet ﷺ had nothing to prepare for him, so he sent to a Jewish man: "Muhammad, Messenger of Allah, says to you: Lend me flour until the new moon of Rajab." He said: "No, unless there is a pledge." I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said: "By Allah, I am trusted by the one in the heavens and trusted by the one on the earth. Were he to lend to me or sell to me, I would certainly repay him." When I had left his presence, this verse was revealed: ﴿Do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to categories of them, the splendour of the worldly life﴾, to the end of the verse [Surah Ta-Ha, 20:131]. It is as if He were consoling him regarding worldly things. [al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/331) by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr, from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, with similar wording, and al-'Iraqi said: "Its chain is weak," because of Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi.]

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Do not extend your eyes﴾, he said: A man was forbidden to wish for the wealth of his companion.

Mujahid said: ﴿toward that by which We have given enjoyment to categories of them﴾ refers to the wealthy.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 15, verses 87–88:

Allah, exalted is He, says to His Prophet: Just as We have given you the Mighty Qur'an, do not look at the worldly life and its adornments, nor at what We have given its people to enjoy, the fleeting splendour, in order to test them through it. Do not envy them for what they have, and do not let yourself be consumed with sorrow (ḥasarāt) over them because of their denial of you and their opposition to your religion. ﴿And lower your wing to the believers who follow you﴾ [Surah al-Shu'ara', 26:215], that is: be gentle and kind toward them, as Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and, toward the believers, kind and merciful﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah, 9:128].

Scholars have differed concerning the *al-Sab' al-Mathani* (the seven oft-repeated): what are they?

Sa'id said: In them Allah has explained the obligatory duties (fara'id), the prescribed punishments (hudud), the narratives (qasas), and the rulings (ahkam).

Ibn 'Abbas said: In them He has explained the parables (amthal), the reports (khabar), and the lessons (ibar).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi 'Umar told us, saying: Sufyan said: *al-Mathani* refers to: al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-Nisa', al-Ma'idah, al-An'am, al-A'raf, and al-Anfal and Bara'ah as one surah.

Al-A'mash said, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was given seven of the long *mathani*, and Musa, peace be upon him, was given six. When he threw down the tablets, two were lifted and four remained.

Mujahid said: They are the seven long surahs. It is also said: They are the Mighty Qur'an.

Khasif said, from Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam, concerning the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿seven of the oft-repeated﴾, he said: I have given you seven parts: commanding, forbidding, giving glad tidings, warning, striking parables, enumerating blessings, and informing you of the news of the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted commands His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to say to the people: I am ﴿the clear warner﴾, clear in warning, a warner to people against a painful punishment that will befall them if they deny him, just as it befell the earlier nations that denied their messengers, and against the punishment and vengeance that Allah sent down upon them.

* *

His saying ﴿al-Muqtasimin﴾ (the dividers/those who swear oaths together) means: those who made pacts with one another, that they would oppose the prophets, deny them and harm them. Allah the Exalted said, reporting about the people of Salih, that they said: ﴿Swear to one another by Allah that we will surely attack him and his family by night﴾ [An-Naml: 49], meaning: we will kill them at night. Mujahid said: "Taqasamu" means they swore an oath to one another.

Allah also said: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die﴾ [An-Nahl: 38]; ﴿Did you not swear before, that for you there would be no decline?﴾ [Ibrahim: 44]; ﴿Are these the ones of whom you swore that Allah would not grant them mercy?﴾ [Al-A'raf: 49]. It was as though they never denied anything without swearing to it, so they were called ﴿muqtasimin﴾.

Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "The Muqtasimun are the companions of Salih, who swore by Allah that they would surely attack him and his family."

In the Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of Bukhari and Muslim), on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "My example and the example of what Allah has sent me with is like that of a man who came to his people and said: 'O people, I have seen the army with my own eyes, and I am the naked warner, so hurry, hurry!' A group among his people obeyed him, set off during the night and departed at their leisure, and they were saved. Another group denied him and remained in their place in the morning, so the army attacked them at dawn, destroyed them and wiped them out. That is the example of whoever obeys me and follows what I have brought, and the example of whoever disobeys me and denies the truth that I have brought."

* *

His saying ﴿Those who made the Qur'an into parts﴾ means: they divided their revealed Books that were sent down to them, believing in some parts and disbelieving in others.

Bukhari said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿They made the Qur'an into parts﴾: "They are the People of the Book; they divided it into portions, believing in some of it and disbelieving in some of it."

[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4705.] [Footnote: In one manuscript, after "and disbelieved in some of it," the following appears: "Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn Abbas, (who made the Qur'an into parts), he said: they are the People of the Book, who divided it into portions, believing in some of it and disbelieving in some of it." This does not appear in Sahih al-Bukhari nor in the rest of the copies, and it is an error.]

Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿As We sent down upon the dividers﴾: "They believed in some and disbelieved in some: the Jews and the Christians."

[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4706.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Similar things have been related from Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak.

Al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿made the Qur'an into parts﴾: "It is sorcery." Ikrimah said: "Al-'Adh-h" means sorcery in the language of Quraysh; they say to a female sorcerer: "innaha al-'adhiha" (she is the sorceress). Mujahid said: "They made it into limbs (a'da'an): they said it is sorcery, they said it is soothsaying, and they said it is the fables of the ancients." Ata' said: "Some of them said: he is a sorcerer; some of them said: he is possessed; and some of them said: he is a soothsayer. That is the 'Idin (parts)." The same was related from al-Dahhak and others.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Sa'id or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who was a man of honor among them, had a gathering of some men of Quraysh around him, and the season (of pilgrimage) had arrived. He said to them: "O assembly of Quraysh, this season has come, and delegations of the Arabs will come to you, and they have heard about the affair of this companion of yours. So agree upon one opinion and do not differ, lest some of you deny others and your statements contradict one another." They said: "You, O Abu Abd Shams, say something and establish for us an opinion that we can hold to." He said: "Rather, you say it, so that I may hear." They said: "We will say he is a soothsayer." He said: "He is not a soothsayer." They said: "Then we will say he is possessed." He said: "He is not possessed!" They said: "Then we will say he is a poet." He said: "He is not a poet!" They said: "Then we will say he is a sorcerer." He said: "He is not a sorcerer!" They said: "Then what shall we say?" He said: "By Allah, his speech has sweetness. Whatever you say of this, it will be recognized as false; and the closest statement is that you say: he is a sorcerer." So they dispersed from him with that, and Allah sent down about them: ﴿Those who made the Qur'an into parts﴾, meaning groups; ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾ [Al-Hijr: 92–93]. The "group" (nafar) who said that about the Messenger of Allah is the one referred to.

Atiyyah al-Awfi said, from Ibn Umar, regarding His saying ﴿We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾: "About 'There is no god but Allah'."

Abdur-Razzaq said: al-Thawri informed us, from Layth (that is, Ibn Abi Sulaym), from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾: "About (the statement) 'There is no god but Allah'."

Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related, through the narration of Shurayk al-Qadi, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ [He said]: "About 'There is no god but Allah'."

[Footnote: Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3126; Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/111). In both of these it comes via the route of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Bashir, from Anas; in Tafsir al-Tabari (14/46) it is related through Shurayk, from Bashir, from Anas. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib (singular) hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym. Abdullah ibn Idris has related, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Bashir, from Anas, something similar, but did not raise it (to the Prophet)."]

Ibn Idris related it from Layth, from Bashir, from Anas, as a mawquf (statement of a Companion, not raised to the Prophet).

[Footnote: Al-Tirmidhi indicated this as mentioned above. Al-Tabari related it in his tafsir (14/46) through Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib, from Ibn Idris, as mawquf.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from Hilal, from Abdullah ibn Ukaym, who said: Abdullah (that is, Ibn Mas'ud) said: "By He other than whom there is no god, none of you will be left alone with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, just as one of you is alone with the moon on the night of the full moon. He will say: 'O son of Adam, what deceived you about Me? O son of Adam, what did you do with what you knew? O son of Adam, how did you respond to the messengers?'"

[Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (14/46).]

Abu Ja'far said, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah: "All the servants will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about two matters: what they used to worship, and how they responded to the messengers."

Ibn Uyaynah said: "about your deed, and about your wealth."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari narrated to us, Yunus al-Hadhdha' narrated to us, from Abu Hamza al-Shaybani, from Ma'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "O Mu'adh, on the Day of Resurrection the believer will be questioned about all of his striving, even about the kohl of his eyes, and about the crumbs of clay on his two fingers. So I will not find you on the Day of Resurrection while anyone is happier with what Allah has given you than you are."

[Footnote: Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah (10/31) through Ishaq ibn Abi Hassan, from Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari, similarly, and it will come in full at the commentary on verse 14 of Surat al-Fajr. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir commented: "A very gharib hadith; in its isnad there is something to be examined, and in its authenticity (there is doubt)."]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾, then He said: ﴿So on that Day, none will be questioned about his sin, man or jinn﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 39]. He said: "He will not ask them, 'Did you do such-and-such?' because He knows that better than they do; rather He will say: 'Why did you do such-and-such?'"

Mujahid said: "They made it into limbs (a'da'an): they said it is sorcery, they said it is soothsaying, and they said it is the fables of the ancients." Ata' said: "Some of them said: he is a sorcerer; some of them said: he is possessed; and some of them said: he is a soothsayer. That is the 'Idin (parts)." The same was related from al-Dahhak and others.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Sa'id or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who was a man of honor among them, had a gathering of some men of Quraysh around him, and the season (of pilgrimage) had arrived. He said to them: "O assembly of Quraysh, this season has come, and delegations of the Arabs will come to you, and they have heard about the affair of this companion of yours. So agree upon one opinion and do not differ, lest some of you deny others and your statements contradict one another." They said: "You, O Abu Abd Shams, say something and establish for us an opinion that we can hold to." He said: "Rather, you say it, so that I may hear." They said: "We will say he is a soothsayer." He said: "He is not a soothsayer." They said: "Then we will say he is possessed." He said: "He is not possessed!" They said: "Then we will say he is a poet." He said: "He is not a poet!" They said: "Then we will say he is a sorcerer." He said: "He is not a sorcerer!" They said: "Then what shall we say?" He said: "By Allah, his speech has sweetness. Whatever you say of this, it will be recognized as false; and the closest statement is that you say: he is a sorcerer." So they dispersed from him with that, and Allah sent down about them: ﴿Those who made the Qur'an into parts﴾, meaning groups; ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾ [Al-Hijr: 92–93]. The "group" (nafar) who said that about the Messenger of Allah is the one referred to.

Atiyyah al-Awfi said, from Ibn Umar, regarding His saying ﴿We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾: "About 'There is no god but Allah'."

Abdur-Razzaq said: al-Thawri informed us, from Layth (that is, Ibn Abi Sulaym), from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾: "About (the statement) 'There is no god but Allah'."

Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related, through the narration of Shurayk al-Qadi, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ [He said]: "About 'There is no god but Allah'."

[Footnote: Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3126; Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/111). In both of these it comes via the route of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Bashir, from Anas; in Tafsir al-Tabari (14/46) it is related through Shurayk, from Bashir, from Anas. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib (singular) hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym. Abdullah ibn Idris has related, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Bashir, from Anas, something similar, but did not raise it (to the Prophet)."]

Ibn Idris related it from Layth, from Bashir, from Anas, as a mawquf (statement of a Companion, not raised to the Prophet).

[Footnote: Al-Tirmidhi indicated this as mentioned above. Al-Tabari related it in his tafsir (14/46) through Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib, from Ibn Idris, as mawquf.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from Hilal, from Abdullah ibn Ukaym, who said: Abdullah (that is, Ibn Mas'ud) said: "By He other than whom there is no god, none of you will be left alone with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, just as one of you is alone with the moon on the night of the full moon. He will say: 'O son of Adam, what deceived you about Me? O son of Adam, what did you do with what you knew? O son of Adam, how did you respond to the messengers?'"

[Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (14/46).]

Abu Ja'far said, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah: "All the servants will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about two matters: what they used to worship, and how they responded to the messengers."

Ibn Uyaynah said: "about your deed, and about your wealth."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari narrated to us, Yunus al-Hadhdha' narrated to us, from Abu Hamza al-Shaybani, from Ma'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "O Mu'adh, on the Day of Resurrection the believer will be questioned about all of his striving, even about the kohl of his eyes, and about the crumbs of clay on his two fingers. So I will not find you on the Day of Resurrection while anyone is happier with what Allah has given you than you are."

[Footnote: Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah (10/31) through Ishaq ibn Abi Hassan, from Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari, similarly, and it will come in full at the commentary on verse 14 of Surat al-Fajr. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir commented: "A very gharib hadith; in its isnad there is something to be examined, and in its authenticity (there is doubt)."]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾, then He said: ﴿So on that Day, none will be questioned about his sin, man or jinn﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 39]. He said: "He will not ask them, 'Did you do such-and-such?' because He knows that better than they do; rather He will say: 'Why did you do such-and-such?'"

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 15, verses 94–99:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to convey what he was sent with, to carry it out, and to proclaim it (al-sad', meaning to confront the polytheists with it). As Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾, it means: carry it out. In another narration: do what you are commanded.

Mujahid said: it means reciting the Qur'an aloud in the prayer.

Abu 'Ubaydah said, from [[In T and A: "Ibn."]] 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: The Prophet ﷺ remained concealed until there was revealed: ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾, and he and his companions then went out. [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/47).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And turn away from the polytheists. Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾ means: convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and do not pay attention to the polytheists who want to turn you away from the signs of Allah. ﴿They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam: 9]. Do not fear them, for Allah is sufficient for you against them and protects you from them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67].

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sakan related to us, Ishaq ibn Idris related to us, 'Awn ibn Kahmas related to us, from Yazid ibn Dirham, who said: I heard Anas [[In T, A, and H: "from Anas, who said: 'I heard Anas,' which is an error; the same occurs in Kashf al-Astar of al-Haythami."]] say concerning this verse: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers who set up with Allah another god﴾.

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by, and some of them gestured at him. Then Jibril came, (I think he said) and he gestured at them, and it entered their bodies like a stabbing, until they died. [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2222, in Kashf al-Astar, and al-Haythami quoted his words: "Yazid ibn Dirham alone transmitted it from Anas, and I know of no one else narrating from Anas other than him." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/46): "In it is Yazid ibn Dirham; Ibn Ma'in weakened him, and al-Fallas declared him trustworthy."]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The chiefs of the mockers, as Yazid ibn Ruman related to me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, were five men, who were of age and honour among their people: from Banu Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qusayy: al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, Abu Zam'ah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as it has reached me, had supplicated against him because of the harm and mockery he caused him, saying: "O Allah, blind his eyes and bereave him of his child." From Banu Zuhrah: al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth ibn Wahb ibn 'Abd Manaf ibn Zuhrah. From Banu Makhzum: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn Makhzum. From Banu Sahm ibn 'Amr ibn Hussays ibn Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy: al-'As ibn Wa'il ibn Hisham ibn Sa'id ibn Sa'd. From Khuza'ah: al-Harith ibn al-Tulatilah ibn 'Amr ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd 'Amr ibn Malkan. When they persisted in evil and increased their mockery of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists. Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, up to His saying: ﴿But they will soon know﴾.

Ibn Ishaq also said: Yazid ibn Ruman related to me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, or from another of the scholars, that Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was circumambulating the House. He stood, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood beside him. Al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib passed by him and threw a green leaf in his face, and he went blind. Al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth passed by him and gestured at his stomach, and his stomach swelled up, and he died of dropsy. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah passed by him and gestured at a wound at the lower part of his ankle. He had been struck by it two years earlier while trailing his lower garment, when he passed by a man from Khuza'ah who was fletching arrows, and an arrow from his quiver caught in his garment and scratched his leg with that scratch, which was nothing; but it festered, and it killed him. Al-'As ibn Wa'il passed by him and gestured at the sole of his foot, and he went out on his donkey heading for al-Ta'if, and it lay down on a thorny plant, and a thorn entered the sole of his foot and killed him. Al-Harith ibn al-Tulatilah passed by him and gestured at his head, and he discharged pus from his nose and died.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from a man, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Their leader was al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and it was he who gathered them.

It has been similarly related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrimah, in a manner similar to the account of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid, from 'Urwah, at length, except that Sa'id says: al-Harith ibn Ghaytalah, and 'Ikrimah says: al-Harith ibn Qays.

Al-Zuhri said: And truly, he is al-Harith ibn Qays, and his mother was Ghaytalah.

Likewise it has been related from Mujahid, Miqsam, Qatadah, and others, that they were five.

Al-Sha'bi said: They were seven.

And the well-known view is the first.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who set up with Allah another god. They will soon know﴾ is a severe threat and a firm warning to whoever associates another object of worship with Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We certainly know that your breast is constricted by what they say. So glorify the praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate﴾ means: Indeed, We know, O Muhammad, that the harm they cause you produces in you constriction and tightness of the chest. Do not let that weaken you, nor let it turn you away from conveying the message of Allah. Rely upon Allah, for He is sufficient for you and will support you against them. So occupy yourself with the remembrance of Allah, praising Him, glorifying Him, and worshipping Him, which is the prayer. For this reason He said: ﴿And be among those who prostrate﴾, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to us, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from Nu'aym ibn Hammar [[In T and A: "'Ammar."]] that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah says: O son of Adam, do not fail to perform four rak'ahs at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you for its end."

Abu Dawud [[In T and A: "Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i."]] related it from the hadith of Makhul, from Kathir ibn Murrah, in a similar form. [[Musnad (5/286) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1289.]]

For this reason, whenever a matter distressed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would pray.

* *

His saying: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾. Al-Bukhari said: Salim said: "The certainty is death." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (8/383), Fath.]]

This Salim is Salim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, as Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Sufyan, Tariq ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to me, from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾, he said: "Death." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/51).]]

Likewise said Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others.

The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He, reporting about the people of the Fire that they said: ﴿We were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the needy, and we used to engage in vain discourse with those who engaged in it, and we used to deny the Day of Recompense, until there came to us the certainty﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 43–47].

In the Sahih, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit, from Umm al-'Ala', a woman of the Ansar, that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon 'Uthman ibn Maz'un after he had died, she said: "May the mercy of Allah be upon you, Abu al-Sa'ib. My testimony concerning you is that Allah has honoured you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "How do you know that Allah has honoured him?" I said: "By my father and mother, O Messenger of Allah, then who?" He said: "As for him, certainty has come to him, and I hope good for him." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1243.]]

From this noble verse, ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾, it is inferred that worship, such as the prayer and the like, is obligatory upon a person as long as his intellect remains intact, so he prays according to his condition, as was established in Sahih al-Bukhari from 'Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then on your side." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1117.]]

It is also used as evidence against those among the heretics (al-malahidah) who held that the meaning of "certainty" is knowledge, so that once one of them attains knowledge, the obligation is dropped from him according to them. This is disbelief, misguidance, and ignorance. The prophets, peace be upon them, and their companions were the most knowledgeable of people about Allah, the most acquainted with His rights and attributes and what He deserves of glorification, and yet they were, along with this, the most devoted to worship and the most constant in performing good deeds until the time of their death. The meaning of "certainty" here is indeed death, as we have already mentioned. To Allah belong praise and grace, and praise be to Allah for guidance, and upon Him we rely and depend, and He is the one asked to cause us to die in the most complete and best of states, for He is Generous and Bountiful.

[And sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.] [[Added from A.]]

This Salim is Salim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, as Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Sufyan, Tariq ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to me, from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾, he said: "Death." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/51).]]

Likewise said Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others.

The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He, reporting about the people of the Fire that they said: ﴿We were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the needy, and we used to engage in vain discourse with those who engaged in it, and we used to deny the Day of Recompense, until there came to us the certainty﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 43–47].

In the Sahih, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit, from Umm al-'Ala', a woman of the Ansar, that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon 'Uthman ibn Maz'un after he had died, she said: "May the mercy of Allah be upon you, Abu al-Sa'ib. My testimony concerning you is that Allah has honoured you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "How do you know that Allah has honoured him?" I said: "By my father and mother, O Messenger of Allah, then who?" He said: "As for him, certainty has come to him, and I hope good for him." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1243.]]

From this noble verse, ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾, it is inferred that worship, such as the prayer and the like, is obligatory upon a person as long as his intellect remains intact, so he prays according to his condition, as was established in Sahih al-Bukhari from 'Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then on your side." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1117.]]

It is also used as evidence against those among the heretics (al-malahidah) who held that the meaning of "certainty" is knowledge, so that once one of them attains knowledge, the obligation is dropped from him according to them. This is disbelief, misguidance, and ignorance. The prophets, peace be upon them, and their companions were the most knowledgeable of people about Allah, the most acquainted with His rights and attributes and what He deserves of glorification, and yet they were, along with this, the most devoted to worship and the most constant in performing good deeds until the time of their death. The meaning of "certainty" here is indeed death, as we have already mentioned. To Allah belong praise and grace, and praise be to Allah for guidance, and upon Him we rely and depend, and He is the one asked to cause us to die in the most complete and best of states, for He is Generous and Bountiful.

[And sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.] [[Added from A.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 15, verses 94–99:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to convey what he was sent with, to carry it out, and to proclaim it (al-sad', meaning to confront the polytheists with it). As Ibn 'Abbas said, regarding ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾, it means: carry it out. In another narration: do what you are commanded.

Mujahid said: it means reciting the Qur'an aloud in the prayer.

Abu 'Ubaydah said, from [[In T and A: "Ibn."]] 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: The Prophet ﷺ remained concealed until there was revealed: ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾, and he and his companions then went out. [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/47).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And turn away from the polytheists. Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾ means: convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and do not pay attention to the polytheists who want to turn you away from the signs of Allah. ﴿They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam: 9]. Do not fear them, for Allah is sufficient for you against them and protects you from them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67].

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sakan related to us, Ishaq ibn Idris related to us, 'Awn ibn Kahmas related to us, from Yazid ibn Dirham, who said: I heard Anas [[In T, A, and H: "from Anas, who said: 'I heard Anas,' which is an error; the same occurs in Kashf al-Astar of al-Haythami."]] say concerning this verse: ﴿Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers who set up with Allah another god﴾.

He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by, and some of them gestured at him. Then Jibril came, (I think he said) and he gestured at them, and it entered their bodies like a stabbing, until they died. [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2222, in Kashf al-Astar, and al-Haythami quoted his words: "Yazid ibn Dirham alone transmitted it from Anas, and I know of no one else narrating from Anas other than him." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/46): "In it is Yazid ibn Dirham; Ibn Ma'in weakened him, and al-Fallas declared him trustworthy."]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The chiefs of the mockers, as Yazid ibn Ruman related to me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, were five men, who were of age and honour among their people: from Banu Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qusayy: al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, Abu Zam'ah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as it has reached me, had supplicated against him because of the harm and mockery he caused him, saying: "O Allah, blind his eyes and bereave him of his child." From Banu Zuhrah: al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth ibn Wahb ibn 'Abd Manaf ibn Zuhrah. From Banu Makhzum: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn Makhzum. From Banu Sahm ibn 'Amr ibn Hussays ibn Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy: al-'As ibn Wa'il ibn Hisham ibn Sa'id ibn Sa'd. From Khuza'ah: al-Harith ibn al-Tulatilah ibn 'Amr ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd 'Amr ibn Malkan. When they persisted in evil and increased their mockery of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists. Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers﴾, up to His saying: ﴿But they will soon know﴾.

Ibn Ishaq also said: Yazid ibn Ruman related to me, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, or from another of the scholars, that Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was circumambulating the House. He stood, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood beside him. Al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib passed by him and threw a green leaf in his face, and he went blind. Al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth passed by him and gestured at his stomach, and his stomach swelled up, and he died of dropsy. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah passed by him and gestured at a wound at the lower part of his ankle. He had been struck by it two years earlier while trailing his lower garment, when he passed by a man from Khuza'ah who was fletching arrows, and an arrow from his quiver caught in his garment and scratched his leg with that scratch, which was nothing; but it festered, and it killed him. Al-'As ibn Wa'il passed by him and gestured at the sole of his foot, and he went out on his donkey heading for al-Ta'if, and it lay down on a thorny plant, and a thorn entered the sole of his foot and killed him. Al-Harith ibn al-Tulatilah passed by him and gestured at his head, and he discharged pus from his nose and died.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from a man, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Their leader was al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and it was he who gathered them.

It has been similarly related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrimah, in a manner similar to the account of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid, from 'Urwah, at length, except that Sa'id says: al-Harith ibn Ghaytalah, and 'Ikrimah says: al-Harith ibn Qays.

Al-Zuhri said: And truly, he is al-Harith ibn Qays, and his mother was Ghaytalah.

Likewise it has been related from Mujahid, Miqsam, Qatadah, and others, that they were five.

Al-Sha'bi said: They were seven.

And the well-known view is the first.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those who set up with Allah another god. They will soon know﴾ is a severe threat and a firm warning to whoever associates another object of worship with Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We certainly know that your breast is constricted by what they say. So glorify the praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate﴾ means: Indeed, We know, O Muhammad, that the harm they cause you produces in you constriction and tightness of the chest. Do not let that weaken you, nor let it turn you away from conveying the message of Allah. Rely upon Allah, for He is sufficient for you and will support you against them. So occupy yourself with the remembrance of Allah, praising Him, glorifying Him, and worshipping Him, which is the prayer. For this reason He said: ﴿And be among those who prostrate﴾, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to us, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from Nu'aym ibn Hammar [[In T and A: "'Ammar."]] that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah says: O son of Adam, do not fail to perform four rak'ahs at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you for its end."

Abu Dawud [[In T and A: "Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i."]] related it from the hadith of Makhul, from Kathir ibn Murrah, in a similar form. [[Musnad (5/286) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1289.]]

For this reason, whenever a matter distressed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would pray.
